eleke: Green and black beads, commonly strung in groups of 7 (or 3)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions. In Yorùbá practice Ògún is honored on Ọjọ́ Ògún of the four-day week and is offered roasted yam and palm oil. Planet, sphere and element are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Alternating red and black beads (some roads of Elegguá use black and white)
timing: Monday, Elegguá's day — and first in any ceremony, before every other Orisha
sacredPlaces: Behind the front door of the home
tools: Otá — consecrated stone or cement head with cowrie-shell eyes
syncretism: The Ánima Sola (Lonely Soul in Purgatory)
element: Not traditionally assigned (keeper of the crossroads)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions, where Elegguá opens and closes every ceremony. In Yorùbá practice Èṣù is Ẹlẹ́gbára, the divine messenger. Planet and sphere are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Alternating red and white beads, commonly in patterns of 6 (or 4)
timing: Friday, Changó's day in Lucumí practice (Wednesday in Candomblé; Ọjọ́ Jàkúta in the Yorùbá week)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions. The third Aláàfin (king) of Ọ̀yọ́ in Yorùbá history. Planet and sphere are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Yellow and amber (gold) beads, commonly grouped in fives
timing: Saturday, Oshun's day in Lucumí practice (Friday in traditional Yorùbá practice)
sacredPlaces: The Ọ̀ṣun River and sacred grove at Òṣogbo, Nigeria
syncretism: Our Lady of Charity of El Cobre (Cuba)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions. Planet, sphere and element are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Blue and clear (crystal) beads, commonly grouped in sevens
timing: Saturday, Yemayá's day in Lucumí practice
sacredPlaces: The Ògùn River at Abẹ́òkúta, Nigeria (her home in Yorùbáland)
temperament: Unforgiving when angered, like the storming sea
syncretism: Stella Maris / Our Lady of Navigators (Brazil)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; her name comes from Yèyé ọmọ ẹja, 'mother whose children are the fish'. Planet, sphere and element are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: All-white beads; some roads add mother-of-pearl, crystal, coral or purple accents
timing: Sunday, Obatalá's day (some houses honor him on Thursday)
temperament: Stern about order, cleanliness and truth
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; in Yorùbá practice Ọbàtálá is also Òrìṣà Ńlá, king of the white cloth. Planet, sphere and element are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Maroon-brown beads with thin black and white stripes, with coral and burgundy crystal; some houses use nine colors
timing: Friday, Oyá's day in Lucumí practice (Wednesday in Yorùbá and Candomblé practice)
temperament: Guardian of the threshold between life and death
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions. Planet, sphere and element are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Alternating green and yellow beads, also worn as the idé bracelet of Orula
timing: Sunday, Orula's day (some houses honor him on Thursday)
sacredPlaces: Palm groves — the sacred palm that yields ikin
Òkè Ìgètí, the hill of Ọ̀rúnmìlà at Ilé-Ifẹ̀
traditionNote: Lucumí conventions, where Orula is served by babalawos. Planet and sphere are modern hermetic cross-references, not part of Orisha tradition.

eleke: Alternating green and yellow beads — the eleke and idé of Orunmila, the Orisha of Ifá
timing: Sunday, Orula's day (some houses honor him on Thursday)
sacredPlaces: Palm groves — the sacred palm that yields ikin
traditionNote: Ifá is the divination system and body of wisdom of Ọ̀rúnmìlà — 16 principal odù yielding 256 in all. Divination itself is reserved for trained babalawos and iyanifa. Planet and sphere are modern hermetic cross-references.

eleke: Royal blue and transparent honey-amber beads, some with coral and jet accents
timing: Monday or Wednesday, and the 4th of each month (many houses honor him on Tuesday with Ogún)
sacredPlaces: Wherever justice is sought — courts and jails
syncretism: Saint Sebastian or Saint George (Brazil, as Oxóssi)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ (his day especially). No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

eleke: White beads striped with blue, with jet and cowrie shells (patterns vary by house)
timing: The 17th of each month, and above all December 17, the feast of San Lázaro
sacredPlaces: Among the sick and the poor
temperament: Severe with those who mock the sick
syncretism: Saint Roch or Saint Lazarus (Brazil, as Obaluaiyê / Omolu)
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ (his weekday especially). No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

eleke: Beads of mixed colors, with green predominant
timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; in the forest, among living plants
temperament: Fair to those who respect the forest
herbs: All plants and leaves are his
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ. No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

eleke: Dark blue with green or white (houses vary: blue, white and black; light green)
timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; at the sea
syncretism: Not syncretized with any saint in Lucumí practice
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ (colors 7 or 9 and form differ widely). No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

eleke: Two necklaces, one red and white (for Changó) and one blue and white (for Yemayá), or mixed
timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; September 26, the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ. No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

eleke: Brown beads combined with nine colors, but no black
timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; July 25, the feast of Saint Christopher
tools: A small figure carried on his shoulder
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ. No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; April 29, the feast of Saint Catherine of Siena
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ. No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.

timing: No weekday is agreed across houses; April 27, the feast of Our Lady of Montserrat
sacredPlaces: The cemetery, among the graves (some houses say its gates)
taboos: Obscenity, quarrelling or immodesty in her presence
traditionNote: Lucumí (Regla de Ocha) conventions; houses and lineages differ (her number is given as 7 or 9). No planet or Western element is traditionally assigned to this Orisha, so none is given.
